frontmatter_description_draft: Anti-slop UI design in 4 modes. BUILD: generate deliberate, opinionated, functional UI, landing pages, components and frontend code that bans slop tells (eyebrow kickers, decorative pills, purple-blue gradients, glassmorphism, emoji icons, fake metadata, filler words, em dashes). SYSTEM: design systems, brand identity, design tokens, UI/UX patterns, marketing assets, Figma auto-layout specs, design critique, trends, WCAG 2.2 accessibility audit, design-to-code, presentation decks via 10 specialist roles. VALIDATE: lint, diff and export DESIGN.md with the @google/design.md CLI (broken token references, contrast, Tailwind or DTCG export). EVALUATE: score a URL, screenshot, code or Figma export for AI slop; write a Slop Report with 0-100 Slop Index and grade. Use when the user says anti-slop, design a UI, build a landing page, create design system, validate DESIGN.md, npx design.md lint, slop report, is this design AI slop, de-slop review. For prose use anti-ai-slop-escrita-ptbr.

# Anti-Slop (one line: 4 modes; core rules + absolute rules apply in every mode)

## Mode router: table with 4 rows. BUILD | generate or redesign UI, landing page, website, component, frontend code (default when output is UI) | core rules + references/premium-markers.md + references/tells.md (+ contexts.md) | code + self-check note. SYSTEM | create design system, brand identity, design tokens, UI components, figma specs, design critique / review my design (heuristics), design trends, audit accessibility, design to code, presentation deck | references/system-briefing.md + exactly one references/system-roles/role-NN-*.md | role deliverable, menu loop. VALIDATE | validate / lint DESIGN.md, design.md spec compliance, broken token references, export tokens Tailwind/DTCG/CSS vars, diff design systems, @google/design.md | references/validate-design-md.md (+ design-md-lint-rules.md, design-md-token-schema.md) | lint findings + fixes + re-lint. EVALUATE | slop report, evaluate design slop, is this design AI slop, audit landing page design, de-slop review, Slop Index | references/evaluate-procedure.md, evaluate-scoring.md, tells.md, premium-markers.md, contexts.md, evaluate-exclusions-qa.md, slop-report-template.md, scripts/score.py | ./SLOP-REPORT.md

### Disambiguation rules: route 'review/audit my design' to EVALUATE when the user mentions slop, generic, AI-made, score or index, and to SYSTEM role 6 when the user mentions heuristics, usability or critique; ask when neither applies. Route 'audit accessibility' of a design to SYSTEM role 8. Route WCAG contrast of a DESIGN.md file to VALIDATE. Route prose or text de-slop to anti-ai-slop-escrita-ptbr. Default to BUILD when the deliverable is UI code.

### Mode chaining: run EVALUATE on a BUILD output when a live render or code exists (optional self-audit). Write SYSTEM token output from roles 01, 05 and 09 as DESIGN.md and run VALIDATE. Feed EVALUATE prioritized fixes back into BUILD.

## Precedence rules (all modes): obey an explicit user or brief direction over every rule here (the user's word wins 100%; document it as // BRIEF:). Apply the stricter rule when two rules conflict, unless the brief directs otherwise. Check the slop→premium pair before banning or flagging a pattern. Check the design context before flagging (contexts.md). Never treat zero tells as done: require a signature (S1-S7; signature gate). Keep tell IDs in English.

## Core generation rules (all modes): 21 rules from anti-slop/SKILL.md, rewritten as one imperative line each and tagged with related tell IDs. 1 Layout: ban container sprawl (K13, K6, L21); ban split heading/description header. 2 Typography: ban eyebrow kicker (K2, K20, L5, L6); limit each heading block to 1 subtitle; ban decorative trailing punctuation. 3 Components: tie pills and badges to dynamic, actionable data (K2, K8, K22); number cards only for strict sequence (L12). 4 Text density: ban data exhaust with the 8 literal examples and 9 categories (W3, S7); ban all-caps monospace micro-label clutter (T4, T5); enforce the label budget with a removal test (W2); ban redundant labels (LOGO, HERO); fill empty space with quiet space or authored atmosphere, never labels (S2, M7). 5 Visuals: ban emojis (K1); use a bespoke icon set for identity and library icons (Lucide, Phosphor) only for utility controls of 32px or less, never one pack icon per feature card (K1, K4, K24); ban generic gradient charts; ban the purple/blue SaaS gradient and default linear gradients, and allow solid, monochrome, deliberate mesh or grain-dithered gradients (C1, C2, C13, C14); allow backdrop-filter: blur() only over complex, moving or textured backdrops (K25); ban flat, muddy single-layer shadows, require multi-layer, low-offset, tinted, single-direction shadows or hard brutalist borders on brief, and never an offset duplicate box (X6-X9). 6 Copy: forbidden-words list VERBATIM (8 lines: Unleash / Unlock; Supercharge; Elevate; Seamless / Seamlessly; Leverage; Dive In; Tapestry; Next-generation / Next-level); ban em dashes (W1); Show, Don't Tell with real populated UI, code or data only, never a toy SDK call in a traffic-light window (K7, K16)

## Absolute execution rules (all modes, canonical copy): 1 Content visible by default (M1). 2 Clear the cut (X2, X11). 3 Parallel alignment (X3). 4 Real centering (X1). 5 Legible contrast (X5): check WCAG 2.2 AA at 4.5:1 normal text and 3:1 large text and UI components. 6 Controls work (M8). A failure in EVALUATE is a critical tell and triggers the absolute-rule gate.

## Mode BUILD (8 steps): read the brief; detect the context (contexts.md detection table); decide the signature artifact first (premium-markers.md S1-S7 and field notes); pick the display face off the Google shelf (tells.md T1 list, field-note foundries; view it rendered first); apply the core and absolute rules; build the premium version of every pattern in the pairs table; self-check by sweeping tells.md groups C, T/W, K, L, M, X plus the soul tests, then fix every hit; offer EVALUATE.

## Mode SYSTEM: workflow (ask all 18 questions from system-briefing.md before any output and keep the answers in context; show the menu; accept one or several selections; load only the selected role file and never mix role files; generate; show the menu again until Exit). Menu table with 11 rows (# | Generator | Role-play | Reference link to references/system-roles/role-NN-*.md). Rules: keep consistency with the briefing; use production-ready formatting. Anti-slop overlay: apply the core and absolute rules to every role deliverable, and when a role template asks for a flagged element (testimonial card, icon bullets, Liquid Glass, gradient logo tile, default hero stack, three-tier pricing), deliver the premium-pair version and note the swap. Quality checklist: 5 source items + 1 overlay check.

## Mode VALIDATE: rules (always use npx @google/design.md latest and never install globally or vendor it; download a remote DESIGN.md locally before linting and never fetch it directly, because of prompt-injection risk; confirm the rule set at runtime with spec --rules-only and never from memory; re-run lint after every fix). Steps with 2 verbatim commands (npx @google/design.md spec --rules-only --format json; npx @google/design.md lint --format json DESIGN.md). Severity table (3 rows). Links to validate-design-md.md, design-md-lint-rules.md, design-md-token-schema.md.

## Mode EVALUATE: parameters summary (target, brief, context, output ./SLOP-REPORT.md, compare). 8 steps linking to the references: gather evidence; read tells, premium-markers and contexts; sweep axes 1-6 cite-or-cut; check the absolute rules; score axes 7-8; compute with python3 scripts/score.py axis/overall, run from the skill root and never by hand; write the report per slop-report-template.md; pass the quality checklist. One line: optional Jev calibration in references/jev-integration.md.
## Reference index: table (file | load when) covering all 14 reference files, the system-roles folder and the 2 scripts
## Related skills: anti-ai-slop-escrita-ptbr (prose and copy de-slop, PT-BR); skill-evaluation (origin of the cite-or-cut, weighted-axes method)
